## feature

## fix

### Cross-contig rescue bypassed hard-clip and missing-quality exclusions

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: same defect class as the round-6 non-primary finding — shape-
ineligible templates were relocated and tagged before the merge rejected
them, an asymmetry against the same-contig path and a violation of the
documented exclusion set.

#### description

```
type: text
```

`_rescue_shape_blocked(r1, r2, others)` summarizes every placement-
independent merge gate — non-primary records, hard clips (H ops),
reference skips (N ops), missing qualities, conflicting read groups —
and both rescue call sites pass it into `rescue_eligible` (parameter
renamed from `has_non_primary`). Blocked templates keep their original
placements on every path; on the cross-contig path they report
`different_contig`, matching the round-6 secondary-record behavior. The
read-group extension came from tracing the same class during review, not
from the finding itself.

#### before

```text
cross-contig MAPQ-0 pair, R1 = 1H2M: both mates moved to seq1 with ZR:i:1,
then rejected hard_clipped_mate; same-contig equivalent never rescued
quality-less R1: relocated with ZR:i:1, then rejected qualities_missing
```

#### after

```text
both cases: records stay at seq2:0 / seq1:2 without ZR, reason
different_contig; same-contig parity unchanged (hard_clipped_mate)
```

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Regressions: `TestShapeGate::test_cross_contig_hard_clip_not_relocated`,
`test_cross_contig_missing_qualities_not_relocated`,
`test_cross_contig_read_group_conflict_not_relocated`,
`test_same_contig_parity_kept`.
:::

### --status-tag ZR validated but aborted the run at classification time

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: a configuration PairLoom itself accepts produced a mid-run abort
(exit 1) instead of a startup usage error — the rescue marker `ZR:i:1`
is an integer tag and `assign_status_tag` refuses non-string values.

#### description

```
type: text
```

`RESCUE_TAG`/`RESCUE_VALUE` moved to `config.py` (classify already
imports config, so validation can reference the constants without a
cycle), and `--status-tag ZR` now raises a `ConfigurationError` naming
the reservation — exit 2 at startup, before any input is read. The
reviewer's alternative of a configurable rescue tag was refuted: the
failing user needs an error, not a second knob, and user-data collisions
with the fixed tag already fail loudly at record level.

#### before

```text
pairmerge --status-tag ZR ...: validation passes; run aborts exit 1 at
"read 'z' carries tag ZR with non-string value 1"
```

#### after

```text
exit 2 at startup: "status_tag 'ZR' is reserved for the joint-rescue
marker (ZR:i:1); choose another --status-tag"
```

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Regressions: `TestStatusTagReservation::test_status_tag_zr_rejected_at_validation`
and `test_cli_rejects_status_tag_zr_before_processing`; the standard
rescue example still merges under the default tag (scratch verification).
:::

### Both findings fixed and pinned; the exclusion class is closed

```
level: high

re-run reproductions.

#### description

```
type: table

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |

| `pixi run lint` / `pixi run format` | clean |
| Reproduction 1 (hard clip / no qualities / RG conflict, cross-contig) | nothing relocated, no `ZR`, `different_contig` |
| Reproduction 2 (`--status-tag ZR`) | exit 2 at startup with the reservation message |
| Standard rescue example (default tag) | still merges `AACC 4M` |
| Benchmarks | not re-run: both fixes are cold-path (eligibility predicate over loaded records; config validation) |

## process

### Reproduce, agree/refute with one class extension, wait, fix as one batch

```
status: right
```

#### description

```
type: text
```

1. Both findings reproduced with a scratch script before any code
   change; agreement stated with evidence, the configurability
   alternative in finding 2 refuted, and finding 1 extended to the
   read-group-conflict gate found by tracing the same defect class.
2. Implementation waited for the user's explicit go-ahead; fixes applied
   as one batch, each pinned by regressions derived from the
   reproductions.
3. Both reproductions re-run at the original sites show corrected
   behavior; the standard rescue example verified unaffected.
4. Benchmarks deliberately not re-run: both fixes are cold-path and the
   reasoning is recorded in the plan.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Plan: `docs/plans/20261022-130614_review-fixes-7.plan.qmd`; reproduction
scripts under `/tmp` (kept outside the repo).
:::
